title: Render Props Basics
description: Understand the render props pattern for component composition.

data.text: The **render props** pattern is a technique for sharing code between components using a prop whose value is a function. The component calls this function instead of rendering its own UI.
A component receives a function as a prop (often called `render` or `children`) and calls it to determine what to render.

data.title: Basic Render Prop

data.text: Instead of a named prop, you can use `children` as the render prop for a more natural JSX syntax.

data.title: Children Render Prop
When to Use Render Props
data.text: Render props are useful when you need to share logic but want the consumer to control the rendering. However, custom hooks have largely replaced this pattern in modern React.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Render props share logic via a function prop
Children can be used as render prop
Custom hooks are often a modern alternative
data.takeaway: Render props enable flexible component composition.
